players.product: 8-inch and 12-inch wafer foundry and technology services (China's largest foundry; fabs in Shanghai, Beijing, Tianjin, Shenzhen)

quarterly_data.quarter: SMIC results announcement: Unaudited Results for the Three Months Ended June 30, 2026 (08-13-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 revenue US$3,005.6 million, up 20.0% QoQ and 36.1% YoY, on higher wafer shipments, higher average selling prices and product mix; gross margin 25.3% (20.1% in Q1 2026, 20.4% in Q2 2025) on higher ASP and mix; profit attributable to owners US$479.2 million. Revenue by region: China 90.2%, America 8.2%, Eurasia 1.6%; 12-inch wafers 78.2% of wafer revenue; by application consumer electronics 44.2%, smartphone 16.9%, industrial and automotive 16.5%, computer and tablet 15.6%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 revenue US$3,005.6 million (+20.0% QoQ, +36.1% YoY); GM 25.3%

quarterly_data.quarter: SMIC results announcement: Unaudited Results for the Three Months Ended June 30, 2026 (08-13-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and utilization: monthly capacity rose to 1,096,500 8-inch-equivalent wafers in Q2 2026 from 1,078,250 in Q1; utilization 93.7% (93.1% in Q1); wafers shipped 2,869,495 8-inch equivalents (+14.4% QoQ, +20.1% YoY); Q2 capex US$1,835.7 million (US$1,562.8 million in Q1).
quarterly_data.figure: Capacity 1,096,500 8-inch-eq wafers/month; utilization 93.7%; Q2 capex US$1,835.7 million

quarterly_data.quarter: SMIC results announcement: Unaudited Results for the Three Months Ended June 30, 2026 (08-13-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management commentary: for H2 2026, the industry push and spillover effects generated by AI will continue, bringing broad demand for IC manufacturing; SMIC is flexibly reallocating existing capacity and quickly qualifying new capacity to help ease tightness in the industry chain, and remains optimistic about the industry and the company.

SMIC.why: China's largest logic wafer foundry (8-inch and 12-inch); management says AI-driven demand and its spillover bring broad demand for IC manufacturing and SMIC is adding capacity to ease industry tightness.
